h: Beginning Bereishit Anew After Simchat Torah
The cycle of Torah reading renews its hidden sweetness and the vitality of Shabbat.
From Simchat Torah to the New Beginning

p: מַתְחִילִין אַחַר שִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה מִ"בְּרֵאשִׁית"
That we begin anew following Simchat Torah from Bereishit
הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּקּוּנִים (תִּקּוּן לו):
is based upon what is written in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 36): "'
יְהִי אוֹר' – דָּא פֶּסַח;
''Let there be light'—this is Passover; '
וַיְהִי אוֹר' – דָּא רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה".
'and there was light'—this is Rosh Hashanah.'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּפֶסַח הָיָה הֲכָנָה לְהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
Meaning that on Passover was the preparation for the revelation of the light of the Written Torah,
שֶׁעִיקַּר הַהִתְגַּלּוּת הָיָה בְּשָׁבוּעוֹת זְמַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה;
whose essential disclosure occurred on Shavuot, the season of the Giving of the Torah;
וּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הֲוָויַּת הָאוֹר,
whereas on Rosh Hashanah is the actualized inception of light,
וְהַיְינוּ אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
namely the light of the Oral Torah,
שֶׁמֵּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מַתְחִיל חִידּוּשׁ אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
for from Rosh Hashanah begins the renewal of the light of the Oral Torah.
דְּאִיתָא בַּתִּקּוּנִים (תִּקּוּן ל):
As taught in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30): "'
יְהִי אוֹר' – דָּא יְמִינָא;
''Let there be light'—this is the Right; '
וַיְהִי אוֹר' – דָּא שְׂמָאלָא".
'and there was light'—this is the Left.'
וְכֵן אִיתָא שָׁם (תִּקּוּן כא):
And so is taught there (Tikkun 21):
מִימִינָא אִתְיְהִיבַת אוֹרַיְיתָא דִּבִכְתָב,
From the Right was given the Written Torah,
וּמִשְּׂמָאלָא אִתְיְהִיבַת אוֹרַיְיתָא דִּבְעַל פֶּה,
and from the Left was given the Oral Torah,
וְכֵן כָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, קסז עַמּוּד א).
and so is written in the holy Zohar (Part II, 167a).
וְהוּא שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל
And this signifies that on Rosh Hashanah following the flaw
הִתְחִיל הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
began the renewal of the Oral Torah,
שֶׁהוּא הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה לְתַקֵּן הָרוֹב כַּעַס.
which represents the increase of wisdom to rectify immense indignation.
וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים נִיתְּנוּ לוּחוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת,
And on Yom Kippur were the second Tablets given,
דְּאִיתָא (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מו, א):
as taught (Shemot Rabbah, parashah 46:1): "
וּבַלּוּחוֹת הַשְּׁנִיּוֹת אֲנִי נוֹתֵן לְךָ שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהֶם הֲלָכוֹת מִדְרָשׁ וְאַגָּדוֹת,
''And in the second Tablets I grant you that there be contained within them Halakhot, Midrash, and Aggadot;
הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב: 'כִּי כִפְלַיִם לְתוּשִׁיָּה'".
this is what is written: 'that sound wisdom is double' (Job 11:6).'
וּבְסֻכּוֹת נִקְבַּע הָאוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And on Sukkot the light of the Oral Torah becomes established
עַל יְדֵי נִיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם וְשִׂמְחַת בֵּית הַשּׁוֹאֵבָה;
through the Water Libation and the Simchat Beit HaShoevah;
וּשְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת – נְבִיעוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא,
and Shemini Atzeret is the wellspring eruption of Torah (nevi'u d'orayta),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שָׁם תִּקּוּן יג).
as written (there, Tikkun 13).

h: The Sweetness Hidden in the Written Torah

p: וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, רמ עַמּוּד א):
And it is brought in the holy Zohar (Part I, 240a): "'
מֵעַז יָצָא מָתוֹק'
– ''Out of the strong came forth sweetness' (Judges 14:14)— '
מֵעַז' דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
'out of the strong' refers to the Written Torah, '
יָצָא מָתוֹק' דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה".
'came forth sweetness' refers to the Oral Torah.'
וְהַיְינוּ דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב נִקְרָא אַרְיֵה,
Meaning that the Written Torah is designated a lion,
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ (בְּרָכוֹת יח:):
and so was expounded (Berakhot 18b): "'
וְהוּא יָרַד וְהִכָּה אֶת הָאֲרִי וְגוֹמֵר' – דִּתְנָא סִפְרָא דְּבֵי רַב",
''and he went down and slew a lion, etc.' (II Samuel 23:20)—that he mastered the Torat Kohanim (Sifra),'
וְהוּא עַל תּוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים;
which pertains to the priestly Book of Leviticus;
וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְתוּל כְּאַרְיֵה,
and the Holy One, blessed be He, is compared to a lion,
דִּכְתִיב: "אַרְיֵה שָׁאָג וְגוֹמֵר".
as it is written (Amos 3:8): 'The lion has roared, etc.'
וּ"מֵעַז יָצָא מָתוֹק"
– And 'out of the strong came forth sweetness'—
הַטַּעַם בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
the experiential taste in the words of Torah,
שֶׁזֶּה עִיקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
which is the foundational essence of the Oral Torah,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וּמְתוּקִים מִדְּבַשׁ וְנֹפֶת צוּפִים",
and regarding this is stated: 'sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb' (Psalms 19:11),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שָׁם.
and as written in the holy Zohar there.
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ (מִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים יט, ז)
And so was expounded (Midrash Tehillim 19:7)
לְשִׁשָּׁה פְּסוּקִים שֶׁקּוֹדֶם לוֹ עַל שִׁשָּׁה סִדְרֵי מִשְׁנָה.
the six preceding verses as corresponding to the Six Orders of the Mishnah.
וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים קיט.):
And this is what they taught in the Gemara (Pesachim 119a): "
הַמְגַלֶּה דְּבָרִים שֶׁכִּסָּה עַתִּיק יוֹמִין,
'One who reveals matters that the Ancient of Days concealed—
וּמַאי נִיהוּ? טַעֲמֵי תוֹרָה",
and what are they? The reasons and inner tastes of the Torah,'
וְהַיְינוּ לִטְעוֹם הַטַּעַם בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
meaning to taste the internal savor in the words of Torah.
וּבְכָל שָׁנָה מַרְגִּישִׁין טַעַם מְחוּדָּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And in every single year one senses a renewed taste in the words of Torah,
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְתִקּוּנִים:
and this is what is written in the holy Zohar and Tikkunim:
ע׳ אַנְפִּין לְאוֹרַיְיתָא,
seventy facets to the Torah,
דִּ"יְמֵי שְׁנוֹתֵינוּ שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה",
corresponding to 'the days of our years are seventy years' (Psalms 90:10),
וְיֵשׁ עוֹד יוֹתֵר פָּנִים לַתּוֹרָה לְמִי שֶׁמַּאֲרִיךְ יָמִים.
and there exist even further facets to the Torah for one who prolongs his days.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין קג:):
And as we find (Sanhedrin 103b):
מְנַשֶּׁה הָיָה שׁוֹנֶה נ״ה (חֲמִשִּׁים וַחֲמִשָּׁה) פָּנִים בַּתּוֹרָה,
King Menashe would expound fifty-five facets in the Torah,
יָרָבְעָם – ק״ג (מֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשָׁה),
and Jeroboam—one hundred and three;
וְהַיְינוּ לְפִי טָעוּתָם שֶׁסָּבְרוּ שֶׁעֲבוֹדָתָם לַשָּׁמַיִם
meaning according to their misconception whereby they presumed their devotions were for Heaven,
דָּרְשׁוּ בְּכָל שָׁנָה פָּנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת בְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים.
they expounded every year a new facet in Torat Kohanim.
אַךְ לְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ ע׳ פָּנִים לִימֵי שְׁנוֹתֵינוּ שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה;
However, for every individual in Israel there are seventy facets corresponding to our seventy years;
וְאַף שֶׁיֵּשׁ יְמֵי הַנְּעוּרִים שֶׁאֵין לוֹ יְדִיעָה כְּלָל בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
and even though there are years of early youth in which one possesses no conscious knowledge of Torah,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מוֹפִיעַ לוֹ בְּכָל שָׁנָה אוֹפֶן מְחוּדָּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
nonetheless there radiates within him every year a renewed dimension in Torah,
כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁמָּצִינוּ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כז, י)
akin to what we find (Vayikra Rabbah, parashah 27:10)
בְּטַעַם מִילָה לִשְׁמוֹנָה,
concerning the reason for circumcision on the eighth day,
וְאֵין מִילָה בְּלֹא שַׁבָּת,
that there is no circumcision without an intervening Shabbat,
שֶׁאַף שֶׁאֵין הַתִּינוֹק מַרְגִּישׁ בִּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
where although the infant does not consciously feel the holiness of Shabbat,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מוֹפִיעַ בּוֹ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִשַּׁבָּת;
nonetheless the sanctity of Shabbat radiates upon him;

h: Seventy Facets in the Word Bereishit

p: וּבַתִּקּוּנִים חָשַׁב ע׳ אַנְפִּין בְּמִלַּת "בְּרֵאשִׁית",
And in the Tikkunim seventy facets were enumerated within the single word Bereishit,
וְהוּא דִּבְמַאֲמַר "בְּרֵאשִׁית" נִכְלָל כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה,
and this is because within the utterance Bereishit the entirety of Creation is encapsulated;
וְכֵן נִקְרְאוּ ז׳ יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית,
and similarly they are designated the 'Seven Days of Creation',
וְהַשַּׁבָּת נִקְרָא שַׁבַּת בְּרֵאשִׁית.
and the Sabbath is titled Shabbat Bereishit.
דִּבְתֵיבַת "בְּרֵאשִׁית" נִכְלָל כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה,
For within the word Bereishit all Creation is contained,
וּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
and the Work of Creation encompasses all words of Torah,
וְשַׁבָּת תַּכְלִית מַעֲשֵׂה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ,
and Shabbat is the ultimate purpose of the creation of heaven and earth,
וְשַׁבָּת כְּלָלָא דְּכֹל אוֹרַיְיתָא,
and Shabbat is the comprehensive summary of the entire Torah;
וְעַל כֵּן דָּרַשׁ ע׳ פָּנִים בְּתֵיבַת "בְּרֵאשִׁית".
and therefore he expounded seventy facets upon the word Bereishit.
וְכֵן יֵשׁ ע׳ פָּנִים בְּכָל תֵּיבָה בְּכָל הַתּוֹרָה.
And so exist seventy facets in every word throughout the entire Torah.

h: The Renewed Taste of Torah on Shabbat

p: וְתֵיכֶף בִּכְנִיסַת שַׁבָּת
And immediately upon the onset of Shabbat
הַזְּמַן לְהַרְגִּישׁ הַטַּעַם הַמְּחוּדָּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
is the auspicious time to perceive the renewed taste in words of Torah.
דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת לא:):
For it is brought in the Gemara (Shabbat 31b):
לֹא בָרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּירְאוּ מִלְּפָנָיו,
The Holy One, blessed be He, created His world solely so that they revere before Him,
וּכְתִיב: "רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה יִרְאַת ה'";
and it is written: 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem' (Psalms 111:10);
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, ה עַמּוּד ב):
and in the holy Zohar (Part I, 5b): "
שַׁבָּת – דְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא אִיהִי יִרְאָה, וְשַׁרְיָא בָּהּ יִרְאָה".
'Shabbat—the eve of Shabbat is fear, and fear abides upon it.'
וְכֵן חָשַׁב הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
And similarly the holy Ari, of blessed memory, accounted
סְעוּדַת לֵיל שַׁבָּת לִקְדוּשַּׁת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
the Friday night meal to the holiness of our father Isaac, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא פַּחַד יִצְחָק,
which is the Dread of Isaac (Pachad Yitzchak),
שֶׁתֵּיכֶף בִּכְנִיסַת שַׁבָּת נוֹפֵל עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל הַפַּחַד וְהַיִּרְאָה.
for immediately upon the arrival of Shabbat there descends upon Israel dread and holy awe.
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה אָנוּ אוֹמְרִים בְּבִרְכַּת מֵעֵין שֶׁבַע
And on this account we recite in the blessing of Me'ein Sheva: "
לְפָנָיו נַעֲבוֹד בְּיִרְאָה וָפַחַד",
'Before Him we shall serve in awe and dread,'
אַף שֶׁבְּבִרְכַּת עֲבוֹדָה לֹא נִזְכַּר יִרְאָה וָפַחַד;
even though in the weekday blessing of Avodah awe and dread are not mentioned;
אַךְ בִּכְנִיסַת שַׁבָּת נוֹפֵל עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל הַפַּחַד וְהַיִּרְאָה.
yet at the entry of Shabbat dread and awe fall upon all Israel.
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ: "אֵימַת שַׁבָּת עַל עַם הָאָרֶץ",
And so they said: 'The dread of Shabbat is upon the unlearned person,'
וְנֶאֱמָן תֵּיכֶף בִּכְנִיסַת שַׁבָּת.
and his testimony is trusted immediately upon the onset of Shabbat.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (יְבָמוֹת ו.):
And this is what they taught in the Gemara (Yevamot 6a): "
לֹא מִשַּׁבָּת אַתָּה מִתְיָירֵא, אֶלָּא מִמִּי שֶׁהִזְהִיר עַל הַשַּׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי";
'You do not fear the Sabbath day itself, but Him Who warned concerning the Sabbath, etc.';
וּמָה רְאָיָה מִשַּׁבָּת, הָא לָא כְּתִיב בָּהּ מוֹרָא?
and what proof is there from Shabbat, seeing that dread is not written explicitly concerning it?
אַךְ שַׁבָּת אִיהִי יִרְאָה, וְשַׁרְיָא בָּהּ יִרְאָה,
Rather Shabbat itself is fear, and fear abides upon it,
רַק הַיִּרְאָה הוּא מִמִּי שֶׁהִזְהִיר עַל הַשַּׁבָּת.
only that the reverence is directed unto Him Who cautioned over the Sabbath.
וְהַזְּמַן לְהַרְגִּישׁ הַטַּעַם הַמְּחוּדָּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And the appointed time to perceive the renewed taste in words of Torah, which is the Oral Torah,
הוּא בְּשַׁבָּת,
is on Shabbat,
דְּכוּלֵי עָלְמָא בְּשַׁבָּת נִתְּנָה תוֹרָה.
for all agree that the Torah was given on Shabbat.
וְקוֹרִין הַפָּרָשִׁיּוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
And we read the weekly portions on Shabbat,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא
wherein there is the disclosure of Atika
לִזְכּוֹת לְאוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא מִטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא.
to merit the light of the Oral Torah which derives from the dew of Atika.
אַךְ נוֹהֲגִין לְהַתְחִיל פָּרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית בְּשִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה,
However, the custom is to commence Parashat Bereishit on Simchat Torah,
שֶׁהוּא שְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
which is Shemini Atzeret in the Land of Israel,
דְּבֵיהּ נְבִיעוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא,
wherein occurs the wellspring eruption of Torah,
שֶׁזֶּה כֹּחַ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהִנְחִיל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּפָרָשַׁת "וְזֹאת הַבְּרָכָה",
which is the power that Moses our teacher bequeathed to Israel in Parashat Vezot HaBerachah,
שֶׁיּוּכַל כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לִזְכּוֹת לְהַרְגִּישׁ הַטַּעַם בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
so that every single Jew can merit to sense the taste in Torah words
שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
which is the core of the Oral Torah;
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרֵאת בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
and therefore it is read on Yom Tov.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁבָּא הַשַּׁבָּת,
And subsequently when Shabbat arrives,
מַתְחִילִין מֵחָדָשׁ בְּפָרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית
we commence anew in Parashat Bereishit
לִזְכּוֹת לְהָאוֹר וְהַטַּעַם הַמְּחוּדָּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה.
to merit the renewed illumination and taste in the Torah.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: and in the holy Zohar (Part I, 5b):

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Introduction 12:82: “There was still one Sabbath left unmentioned. Feeling humiliated, she pleaded before the Creator, saying, “O Lord of the universe, since the time when Thou didst create me, I have been called merely ‘day of Sabbath’, but surely a day must have for companion a night.” Said the Lord to her, “O my daughter, thou art Sabbath, and Sabbath I will call thee. But I will confer on thee an even more glorious crown.” He then made proclamation, “And ye shall fear my sanctuary” (Ibid.). This is a reference to the Sabbath of the eve of Sabbath, which inspires fear, and upon which fear rests. And it is the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself who identified Himself with her, saying “I am the Lord” (Ibid.). I have further heard’ (continued the stranger) ‘the following exposition from my father. He stressed the particle eth as signifying the limit of the Sabbath walk. “My Sabbaths,” he said, denotes the circle and the square within, and corresponding to these two the sanctification recital consists of two parts, one the verses Genesis 2, 1-3, commencing Vaikhulu (and were completed) and the other the sanctification proper (Kiddush). Vaikhulu contains thirty-five words, and the Kiddush contains thirty five words, making together seventy, corresponding to the seventy names of the Holy One, blessed be He, by which the congregation of Israel is crowned.”

paragraphs.text: Sefat Emet, Deuteronomy, Sukkot 9:8: “Therefore we celebrate Simchas Torah, to accept the yoke of Torah with joy, so that this acceptance will remain throughout all the days of the year. In truth, the essential vitality of everything comes through Torah, as is said: “Bereishis”—for the sake of Torah, which is called “reishis.” The Midrash explains, “I was beside Him as an amon”—an artisan: He looked into Torah and created the world. It says, “I was,” for each and every year a new manner of Divine governance is renewed through the power of Torah. Concerning this it says, “The eyes of Hashem your God are upon it from the beginning of the year”: through Torah, which is called “reishis,” and through the Children of Israel, who are called “reishis.” The Creator's providence operates through the power of Torah found within Israel. According to the measure of Torah's power found within Israel, the year is renewed. I likewise heard from my grandfather and teacher, of blessed memory, his explanation of the verse, “Understand the years of generation after generation”: in each and every year there is a new understanding in Torah.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: לכן עושין שמחת תורה לקבל עול תורה בשמחה להיות נשאר הקבלה על כל ימי השנה. כי באמת עיקר חיות הכל ע"י התורה כמ"ש בראשית בשביל התורה שנק' ראשית. ובמד' ואהי' אצלו אמון אומן שהביט בתורה וברא העולם. וכתיב ואהי' שכן מתחדש בכל שנה ושנה הנהגה חדשה בכח התורה. וע"ז כתיב עיני ה' אלקיך בה מראשית השנה. ע"י התורה שנק' ראשית וע"י בנ"י שנק' ראשית. שהשגחת הבורא ית' בכח התורה שנמצא בבנ"י. וכפי ערך כח התורה שנמצא בבנ"י כך מתחדשת השנה. וכן שמעתי מפי אא"ז מו"ר ז"ל פ' הפסוק בינו שנות דור ודור שיש בכל שנה ושנה הבנה חדשה בתורה:
